(a) Assessments for wastes exceeding authorized concentrations; enumeration. If the city authorizes any customer to discharge industrial wastes into the public sewers, such customer shall be charged and assessed a surcharge in addition to any sewer service charges if these wastes have a concentration greater than the following concentrations, which represent a relatively high strength domestic-type wastewater:
(1) A five-day, 20 degrees Celsius biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of 250 milligrams per liter (mg/l), which is also referred to as parts per million (ppm).
(2) A suspended solids content of 250 mg/l.
(3) For wastewater discharging to a treatment plant where nitrification is required, a total Kjeldahl nitrogen (TKN) and/or ammonia (NH3-N) of seven mg/l (separately or in combination).
(4) For wastewater discharging to a treatment plant where phosphorus treatment is required, phosphorus and phosphorus compounds (as P) of 25 mg/l.
Such constituents shall be sampled and analyzed in accordance with Standard Methods or other analytical procedure approved by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency or the regulatory agency of the state having jurisdiction. The surcharge shall be based on an average of at least three 24-hour composite samples (or composite samples during the daily discharge); or based on an average of at least six grab samples taken at different hours of operation over at least a three-day period. Where different processes are used or different products are manufactured, the highest strength discharge over a five-day period, as sampled above, shall be used as the basis of the surcharge. The amount of such surcharge, which may be charged and assessed against persons discharging industrial waste into the public sewers, shall reflect the cost incurred by the city in handling the excess of the previously listed constituents. This surcharge shall include a proportionate share of the operational and maintenance costs and replacement costs on the portions of the plant and affected sewer system and other incidental expenses (monitoring, testing and other).
(b) Formulas for calculating surcharges. When any or all of the total suspended solids, BOD, phosphorus, TKN or ammonia of the wastewater accepted for admission to the city's sewer works exceeds the values described in subsection (a) of this section of these constituents, the excess concentration in any or all, as the case may be, shall be subject to a surcharge on the amount derived in accordance with the following formula:
Amount of surcharge in dollars = (pounds of excess constituent) × (prorated facility replacement cost per excess pound + prorated operational, maintenance and incidental costs per excess pound)
Excess poundage shall be figured as follows:
(Wastewater discharged in gallons × excess concentration in mg/l × 8.34 lbs./gallons) divided by 1,000,000.
Example:
1,000,000 gallons of wastewater
250 mg/l excess BOD (500 mg/l - 250 mg/l)
Then:
Excess poundage = 1,000,000 × 250 × 8.34 1,000,000
(c) Review of surcharge rates. The rates of surcharges shall be reviewed annually by the city in order that the factors in subsections (a) and (b) of this section may correctly represent current treatment costs and may be modified at any time.
(d) Billing; right of city to inspect, sample and test. Industrial waste surcharges provided for in this division shall be prepared and rendered with the regular water and sewer bill. The city's water and wastewater superintendent or other duly authorized employee of the city shall be permitted to enter upon any properties for the purpose of inspection, observation, measuring, sampling, and testing in accordance with the provisions of this article.
(e) Computation based on water consumption. The volume of flow used to compute industrial waste surcharges shall be based upon metered, estimated or prorated water consumption as shown in the records of meter reading maintained by the city. If a person discharging waste into the public sewer system produces evidence to the city that a significant portion of the total annual volume of water used for all purposes does not reach the public sewer system, an estimated percentage of total water consumption to be used in computing charges may be agreed upon between the city and persons discharging industrial waste into the sewer.
(f) Annual inspection; determination of character and concentration of waste; methods. The industrial waste of each person, corporation or legal entity discharging such waste into the public sewer system shall be subject to annual inspection and determination of character and concentration of such waste. Such action may be made more often as may be deemed necessary by the city. Samples shall be collected in such a manner as to be representative of the actual quality of the waste. The laboratory methods used in examination of the waste shall be those set forth in Standard Methods.
(g) Dispute over analysis; resampling and gauging procedure. If an analysis of waste, determined by the sampling and gauging of waste from a person or industry by the city, is disputed, a program of resampling and gauging, with subsequent chemical determinations, may be instituted as follows:
(1) The person or industrial user interested must submit a request for resampling and gauging of their waste to the city by letter and bind themselves to bear the expenses incurred by the city in the resampling and gauging the subsequent chemical determination of the waste.
(2) The chemist or engineer employed by the company or person responsible for the request submitted to the city must confer with the city's person in charge of gauging and sampling. They will establish the length of the rerun and the methods to be employed to determine the flow and to sample the flow.
(3) The chemist or engineer engaged by the person or industry may be present during the gauging and sampling operation and also in the laboratory during the determination of the analysis.
(4) The results of the analysis, determined from the quantity and quality of the flow, shall be considered by analysis of record.

(2) Any waters containing toxic or poisonous solids, liquids, or gases in sufficient quantity, either singly or by interaction with other substances, to injure or interfere with any waste treatment process, constitute a hazard to humans or animals, create a public nuisance, or create any hazard in the receiving waters of the wastewater treatment plant.

The city may set limitations lower than the limitations established in the regulations in this section if, in its opinion, such more severe limitations are necessary to meet the objectives of this section. In forming its opinion as to the acceptability, the city will give consideration to such factors as the quantity of subject waste in relation to flows and velocities in the sewers; materials or construction of the sewer; the wastewater treatment process employed and wastewater discharge requirements; capacity of the wastewater treatment plant; degree of treatability of the waste in the wastewater treatment plant; and the toxicity of the pollutant, its persistence, degradability and other pertinent factors. (1) Any liquid or vapor having a temperature higher than 150 degrees Fahrenheit (65 degrees Celsius).
(2) Wastewater containing more than 25 milligrams per liter of petroleum oil, nonbiodegradable cutting oils, or products of mineral oil origin.
(3) Wastewater from industrial plants containing oils, fats, or grease in excess of 100 milligrams per liter.

(10) Any waters or wastes having suspended solids contents in excess of 250 milligrams per liter (mg/l) by weight on a 24-hour composite basis, except as otherwise permitted with a surcharge.
(11) Where nitrification treatment is required, any waters or wastes having total Kjeldahl nitrogen or ammonia (separately or in combination) in excess of 25 milligrams per liter (mg/l) by weight on a 24-hour composite basis, except as otherwise permitted with a surcharge.

(16) Waters or wastes colored by dye or other such solutions to such a degree that the color is not sufficiently removed by treatment to cause problems or adverse effects to receiving water.
(17) Any contaminant which the city or its designated agent deems harmful to the operation or efficiency of wastewater treatment plants, or to the health and welfare of the residents of the city.
(18) Ground paper products shall be prohibited from being discharged into the public sewer system, unless otherwise approved by the city.
(19) Discharge of materials or substances which would cause the effluent quality from sewage treatment plants to violate state and federal standards.
(20) Any discharge at a temperature which will cause the temperature of the wastewater in the sewer system to increase to 120 degrees Fahrenheit, or above.
(21) Any other circumstances that from time to time may be listed by the city.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 505, 4-5-1994)
1027:
If any waters or wastes are discharged or are proposed to be discharged to the public sewers, which waters contain the substances or possess the characteristics enumerated in sections 64-138 and 64-139, and which, in the judgment of the city, may have a deleterious effect upon the wastewater facilities, processes, equipment or receiving waters, or which otherwise create a hazard of life or constitute a public nuisance, the city may:
(1) Discontinue service and/or reject the wastes;
(2) Require pretreatment to an acceptable condition for discharge to the public sewers;
(3) Require control over the quantities and rates of discharge; and/or
(4) Require payment to cover added costs of handling and treating the wastes not covered by existing taxes or sewer charges under the provisions of section 66-148.
If the city permits the pretreatment or equalization of waste flows, the design and installation of the plants and equipment shall be subject to the review and approval of the city, and of the environmental protection division, department of natural resources of the state, and other regulatory agencies having jurisdiction. If the owner or operator is not in compliance, the city will grant a reasonable time period for the owner or operator to take corrective measures before service is discontinued. An owner or operator of any source to which the pretreatment standards are applicable shall comply with 40 CFR 403, as the same may, from time to time, be amended or replaced.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 506, 4-5-1994)
1028:
Any industrial "new source" (as defined in Public Law 92-500, section 316 (33 USC 3161) as the same may, from time to time, be amended or replaced) contributed to the publicly owned wastewater treatment works shall comply with the requirements of such cited statute and the regulations promulgated thereunder (40 CFR 403 as the same may, from time to time, be amended or replaced) establishing federal standards of performance for new sources within the contributor's particular category.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 507, 4-5-1994)
1029:
Any industrial source of pollutants shall comply with the effluent standards or prohibition of each designated pollutant or combination of pollutants as established by Public Law 92-500, section 307 (33 USC 1317, as the same may, from time to time, be amended or replaced) and the regulations promulgated thereunder. Furthermore, any industrial source of pollutant shall comply with the pretreatment standards for introduction of pollutants into publicly owned treatment works as established by Public Law 92-500, section 307 (33 USC 1317, as the same may, from time to time, be amended or replaced) and the regulations promulgated thereunder, for those pollutants which are designated by the federal regulations as being unsusceptible to treatment by such treatment works or which would interfere with the operation of such treatment works.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 508, 4-5-1994)
1030:
Any industrial user or source which is required to comply with the standards of performance effluent standards or pretreatment standards established by Public Law 92-500, sections 306 and 307, and the federal regulations promulgated thereunder shall further comply with the inspection, monitoring and entry requirements of Public Law 92-500, section 308 (33 USC 1317) and the federal regulations promulgated thereunder.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 509, 4-5-1994)
1031:
Grease, oil and sand interceptors shall be provided when in the opinion of the city, they are necessary for the proper handling of liquid waste containing floatable grease in excessive amounts, as specified in section 66-139(3), or any flammable wastes, sand, any substance which becomes viscous or solidifies at a temperature above 32 degrees Fahrenheit (0 degrees Celsius) or other harmful ingredients; except that such interceptors shall not be required for private living quarters or dwelling units. All interceptors shall be of a type and capacity approved by the city, and shall be located as to be readily and easily accessible for cleaning and inspection. In the maintaining of these interceptors, the owner shall be responsible for the proper removal and disposal by appropriate means of the captured material and shall maintain records of the dates and means of disposal which are subject to review by the city. Any removal and hauling of the collected materials not performed by the owner's personnel must be performed by currently licensed waste disposal firms. A copy of all disposal records, including dates of cleaning and disposal of collected materials, means of disposal, and place of disposal, must be furnished to the city by any such waste disposal firm each time an interceptor is cleaned.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 510, 4-5-1994; Ord. No. 99-5, § 1, 5-4-1999)
1032:
Where pretreatment or flow-equalizing facilities are provided or required for any waters or wastes, they shall be maintained continuously in satisfactory and effective operation by the owner at his expense. The owner shall submit operation and laboratory data on a monthly basis to the city. The city or EPD shall determine the proper procedures.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 511, 4-5-1994)
1033:
When required by the city, the owner of any property serviced by a building sewer carrying industrial wastes shall install a suitable structure, together with such necessary meters and other appurtenances, in the building sewer to facilitate observation, sampling, and measurement of the waste by the city. Such structure, when required, shall be accessible and safely located and shall be constructed in accordance with plans approved by the city. The structure shall be installed by the owner at his expense and shall be maintained by him so as to be safe and accessible at all times.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 512, 4-5-1994)
1034:
All measurements, tests, and analyses of the characteristics of waters and wastes to which reference is made in this article shall be determined in accordance with the latest edition of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, published by the American Public Health Association. Sampling methods, location, times, durations, and frequencies are to be determined on an individual basis, subject to approval by the city.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 513, 4-5-1994)
1035:
No statement contained in this article shall be construed as preventing any special agreement or arrangement between the city and an industrial concern whereby an industrial waste of unusual strength or character may be accepted by the city for treatment. The city may levy a surcharge for the treatment of such waste.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 514, 4-5-1994)
1036:
In the event of an accidental spill or an unavoidable loss to the drains of any deleterious material or substances, the person concerned shall promptly inform the manager, or the city's designated agent, of the nature, quantity and time of occurrence of the spill. The person concerned shall take all possible actions to prevent a spill, and should a spill occur, shall take immediate steps to ensure no recurrence of the spill. Where there exists an approved drain to the sanitary sewer in an area where there is the potential for a leak or spill of toxic, flammable material or harmful substance an emergency block valve on the sanitary sewer downstream of the aforementioned drain shall be required.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 515, 4-5-1994)
1037:
Any person, upon written application to the city, who shows, in the case of the activity being conducted or operated, that compliance with a section of this article would either be impossible or would constitute an undue hardship because of time limitations, may be granted a variance. If a variance is granted by the city, it shall be only for such reasonable period of time as determined by the city under the specified conditions set by the city. If the person to whom the variance is granted fails to comply with the specifications of the city within the time set, the city shall have the right to revoke the variance granted and terminate all service (water and wastewater and sewer) to the customer until all requirements of the city have been complied with. A variance shall not be granted under the provisions of this section where the person applying therefor is causing a nuisance or other injury to the public. Any variance granted under the provisions of this section shall not relieve the person receiving the variance from any liability or penalties imposed by law for the commission or maintenance of a public nuisance.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 516, 4-5-1994)
1038:
No person shall discharge or empty any contents of septic tanks and portable toilets into the wastewater system of the city.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 517, 4-5-1994)
1039:
Should a customer (user) be found to be in violation of the restrictions on public sewer use as provided in this division, the city may take appropriate action to terminate the customer's water and sewer service until such time as the violation is abated and payment is made to the city for any damages caused thereby to the sewer system.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 518, 4-5-1994)
1040:
Should any person who is not a customer of the city be found in violation of the restrictions on public sewer use as provided in this division, the city may take appropriate action to have civil and/or criminal action taken against such person violating the terms of this article.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 519, 4-5-1994)
1043:
Any owner/developer desiring sewer service to his property shall deliver to the city a plat of survey of the property to be sewered along with a letter setting forth the intended uses of the property.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 1101, 4-5-1994)
1044:
The owner/developer of the property will be required to construct, at his own expense, any and all sewer lines and sewer facilities that are located on the owner/developer's property that are determined by the city to be needed for the adequate sewering of the property or that are required to service the owner/developer's property.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 1102, 4-5-1994)
1045:
The owner/developer will employ its own contractor to construct the sewer lines from the owner/developer's property to the city's nearest facilities having capacity to process the sewage generated from such property. The sewer lines, appurtenances thereto, and other facilities required will be constructed according to the specifications of the city and will be inspected by the city prior to covering. The contractor shall deliver to the city prior to the commencement of work a certificate of insurance which will insure and protect the city from all claims of damage to person or property occurring as a result of the construction.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 1103, 4-5-1994)
1046:
If the city determines that it is in the best interest of the city to enlarge the sewer lines and sewer system facilities from the owner/developer's property line to the sewer system facilities, the owner/developer shall be responsible for 100 percent of the cost for the increased size of sewer line and sewer facilities.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 1104, 4-5-1994)
1047:
The owner/developer shall make a good faith effort to obtain all easements required to install the sewer lines from the owner/developer's property to city's facility. In the event an owner/developer is unable to obtain the sewer easements required, the owner/developer shall notify the city in writing. The city will then determine the anticipated costs for condemning the easements required and notify the owner/developer in writing. Upon the owner/developer depositing with the city the estimated costs, the city will authorize its attorney to proceed with condemnation of the easement. If the costs exceed the amount estimated by the city, the owner/developer shall pay to the city the additional costs within ten days from the receipt of notification. Failure to pay such funds within the allotted time will result in the city placing a fi. fa. upon owner/developer's property. If estimated costs paid to the city exceed the actual costs incurred, the excess funds will be returned to the person initially paying the funds within 30 days after date of determination of actual costs involved. Costs shall include, but not be limited to, the amount paid by the city for the easement or title to property, all attorneys' fees, expert witness fees, court costs, litigation expenses and any out-of-pocket funds expended by the city.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 1105, 4-5-1994)
1048:
The city will employ its own surveyor or engineer to survey the property upon which the easement or title to property is required to carry the sewer line from the owner/developer's property to the city's existing facility. An estimated cost of such expense will be provided by the city to the owner/developer in writing, and the owner/developer shall deposit such funds with the city. Upon receipt of the estimated costs, the city will proceed to survey the property and have the easements prepared by the city's attorney. If the costs exceed the amount estimated by the city, the owner/developer shall pay to the city the additional costs within ten days from the receipt of notification. Failure to pay the funds within the allotted time will result in the city placing a fi. fa. upon the owner/developer's property. If estimated costs paid to the city exceed the actual costs incurred, the excess funds will be returned to the person initially paying such funds within 30 days after the date of determination of actual costs involved. Costs shall include, but not be limited to, the amount paid by the city for the easement or title to property, all attorney's fees, expert witness fees, court costs, litigation expenses and any out-of-pocket funds expended by the city.
(Ord. No. 94-4, § 1106, 4-5-1994)
1050:
Footnote 3:
Cross reference— Water conservation, § 34-201 et seq.
1051:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
City means the mayor and city council of the city, and its agents and employees.
Consumer means any person, corporation, partnership, joint venture or public body that uses, has use of, has use for or seeks to use water furnished by the city or its agents.
Developer means any person, corporation, partnership, joint venture, public body or legal entity that is selling, offering for sale, dividing, subdividing or developing property for residential, commercial or industrial use.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 1, 5-7-1996)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
1052:
The city shall enforce the terms of this article through the administrative procedures set out in this article through legal actions in a court of law.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 14, 5-7-1996)
1053:
(a) Initial application. Any consumer or developer desiring to be provided water services through the city's water lines shall make an application for water services in person at city hall. The owner of the property or structure to be served is responsible for the application.
(b) Line availability. If the water distribution system includes a water line adjacent to, or directly across the road from, the consumer's property, and no water line extension is required, service will be provided upon the customer executing a service contract and paying the required service connection fee and meter installation fee.
(c) Enlargement of water lines; costs. If the city determines that it is in the best interest of the city to enlarge the water lines and water system facilities from the owner/developer's property line to the water system facilities, the owner/developer will be responsible for 100 percent of the costs for the increased size of water line and water facilities.
(d) Installation list. Upon complying with subsections (a) and (b) of this section, the consumer will be placed on the meter installation list. The connection and the meter will be installed by the city, or its agent, as soon as practicable thereafter.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 2, 5-7-1996; Amend. of 6-3-1997, § 12)
1054:
(a) Water connection line. Upon the consumer meeting the requirements of section 66-223, the city will run a water connection line to the property of the consumer. The water connection will include a curb stop valve, meter and meter box. In addition, a pressure reducer will be installed when average line pressure at the connection exceeds 90 psi.
(b) Site of meter. The city may install its meter at or near the property line, or at the city's option, on the consumer's property within three feet of the property line.
(c) Initiation of service. When the consumer has connected his piping to the meter, the city will inspect the connection and turn on water service. Under no circumstances shall the consumer operate the curb stop valve on the downstream side of the meter.
(d) Right to refuse service. The city reserves the right to refuse service unless the consumer's lines and piping are installed in conformity with the city's specifications and the regulations of the current plumbing code in the city and the county.
(e) Interruptions of service. Under normal conditions, the consumer will be notified of any anticipated interruptions of service by the city.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 3, 5-7-1996)
1055:
(a) Water use. Water furnished by the city shall be used for consumption by the consumer, members of the household, employees and/or visitors only. The consumer shall not sell water to any other person or permit any other person to use said water. The consumer shall not allow anyone else to connect onto the water system serving the consumer. Water shall not be used for irrigation, or other purposes, except when water is available in sufficient quantity without interference with the regular domestic consumption in the area served. Disregard of this rule shall be sufficient cause for refusal and/or discontinuance of service.
(b) Access to meter. Where the meter or meter box is placed on the premises of a consumer, a suitable place shall be provided by the consumer therefor, which is unobstructed and accessible at all times to the meter reader.
(c) Consumer's cut-off valve. The consumer shall furnish and maintain a private cut-off valve on the consumer's side of the meter within the meter box.
(d) Backflow prevention device. The consumer's piping and apparatus shall be installed and maintained by the consumer at the consumer's expense so as to prevent a backflow by use of an approved backflow prevention device. Under normal conditions, the backflow prevention device must be located within the meter box to allow for regular testing of its functioning.
(e) Pressure release device. The consumer shall furnish and maintain an approved pressure relief device on a cold water line on the consumer's side of the meter. This pressure relief device shall not be located in the meter box.
(f) Disconnection of wells.
(1) No physical connection. In order to be received as a consumer and entitled to receive water from the city's water system, all applicants must offer proof that any private wells located on their property are not physically connected to the lines of the city's water system. All applicants, by becoming consumers of the city, covenant and agree that, so long as they continue to be consumers of the city, they will not permit the connection of any private wells to the authority's water system.
(2) Sealing of certain wells. In areas designated on an individual lot-by-lot basis, all existing wells must be disconnected, filled, sealed and plugged from further use, in accordance with the state department of natural resources and county board of health regulations, and no new wells may be bored or drilled.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 4, 5-7-1996)
1056:
Duly authorized agents and employees of the city shall have access at all reasonable hours to the premises of the consumer and/or property owner for the purposes of installing and removing the property of the city, inspecting the city's facilities, reading and testing meters and repairing and maintaining the facilities of the city.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 5, 5-7-1996)
1057:
(a) Charges for initial water service. Each consumer subscribing for uses of water services through the city shall pay a nonrefundable connection fee. (See appendix to Ordinance No. 96-4 and 96-10 for charges.)
(b) Meter for each unit. A separate meter is required for each individual dwelling unit and/or unit of business. All multiunit commercial or professional buildings shall have a meter installed for each unit. All multifamily dwellings shall have a meter installed for each unit. The prevailing service connection fee and meter installation fee shall be paid for each unit.
(c) Fire line installation. All individual dwelling units and/or units of business including all multiunit commercial or professional buildings that require fire installation must install a meter or backflow preventer or a detection check valve. All consumers who install a fire line will be required to pay the minimum monthly charge as set by the city commencing on the next billing date after the meter and a backflow preventer or a check detection valve are set and water is available. (See appendix to Ordinance No. 96-4 and 96-10 for charges.)
(d) Deposits. The city is authorized to establish deposit fees to be paid for water and sewer service and to collect such fees upon application for service and at such other times as the city may determine to be necessary. For rental property, tenants will be required to pay the established deposit fee. When a tenant moves out, the deposit, less any amount owed, will be refunded to the tenant. If service is not shut off at the meter, a regular deposit will be required from the property owner. (See appendix to Ordinance No. 96-4 and 96-10 for charges.)
(e) Water rates. The rate schedule used for the city is set from time to time. However, water rates will not increase without 30 days' notice to the consumer. Notice will be sufficiently given to the consumer by a publication of the rate changes at least one time in the official newspaper of the county prior to the rate increase. Property owners shall be responsible for any unpaid water bills. (See appendix A to Ordinance No. 96-10 for current rates.)
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 6, 5-7-1996; Amend. of 6-3-1997, §§ 13—17)
1058:
(a) Reading schedule. The water meter serving the consumer's property shall be read on a monthly basis and official records of each reading thereof shall be kept for a period of one year.
(b) Meter designation. Water meters shall be classified as either active meters, inactive meters and canceled meters. These designations are defined as follows:
(1) Active meters are defined as meters that are in normal use. All active meters will be charged on a monthly basis.
(2) Inactive meters are defined as meters that are installed where the consumer has notified the city in writing to temporarily terminate service. When it receives such written request, the city will seal the meter and declare the meter an inactive meter. When no responsible party is available to request inactive meter designation for the consumer, the city may declare the meter inactive. If a consumer desires to obtain water services after the meter has been declared inactive, the consumer shall pay the city a deposit and reconnection fee. In addition, the consumer must pay any previous unpaid bills which that consumer had through the city's services prior to obtaining any additional service from the city. Once the deposit, connection fee and any past due bills have been paid, the meter will be reclassified as an active meter as defined in subsection (b)(1) of this section.
(3) Canceled meters are defined as meters that have not been in use where the consumer has notified the city that no further water service from the city is desired. The city may, on its own initiative, declare a meter canceled when water has not been used for a period of 12 months or longer, excluding fire lines. If a meter is declared a canceled meter, the meter will be removed and the connection sealed. A consumer desiring reconnection of a canceled meter shall pay the deposit and connection fee that is in effect as of the date of application.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 7, 5-7-1996)
1059:
(a) Payment. The consumer shall pay promptly on a monthly basis for all water registered by the meter serving such property at the rates set by the city from time to time, which shall include water used, water wasted or leakage, except for the water that may be traced by the city to the city's system.
(b) Billing schedule. Bills are sent out on the first day of each month. Bills shall be paid by the tenth day of each month. Payments received after the tenth will be assessed a ten percent late fee. If no payment is received, service will be discontinued on the 21st day of the month. If water service is disconnected for nonpayment of the bill, the city will not resume water service to the consumer until the bill, reconnection fees and all penalties have been paid in full. If the tenth day of the month falls on a Saturday, Sunday or a holiday, when city hall is closed, payments will be accepted without late charge on the following workday when city hall is open.
(c) Billing errors. If the consumer believes his bill to be in error, this claim must be presented to the city, or its billing agent, before the bill becomes due. Such claim, if made after the bill has become delinquent, shall not be effective in preventing discontinuance of service as provided in this section. The customer may pay such bill under protest and such payment shall not prejudice his claim. Any consumer who fails to notify the city in writing within 30 days after the date of such bill of any irregularities or errors that may be in such bill shall waive any right or claim for correction or refund under such bill.
(d) Meter failure. If the seal of a meter is broken by any person other than the city's representative, or if the meter fails to register correctly, or is stopped for any cause, the consumer shall pay an amount which is the average for the preceding month's water usage.
(e) Meter testing and rechecks. The city will carry out a regular program of meter testing and replacement. In addition, water meters will be tested at the request of the consumer. The city may make a charge for a consumer requested meter recheck. (See appendix to Ordinance No. 96-4 and 96-10 for charges.)
(f) Fee for bad checks. Consumers who make payments with checks which are not covered by sufficient funds will be charged a bad check fee as set by the city. When a consumer has written a check which has been returned for insufficient funds, the city will accept only cash or money orders for the next 12 months.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 8, 5-7-1996; Amend. of 6-3-1997, § 17)
1060:
(a) Refund of deposit. When water service is discontinued either by written notice from the consumer to the city, or by acts of the city, or its agents, the city shall apply any refundable deposits held to the balance of the bill owed by the consumer and refund the difference, if any exists, to the consumer. The city will not add accrued interest earned to any consumer refunds.
(b) Termination without notice. The city reserves the right to discontinue its service without notice for the following reasons:
(1) For emergency repairs.
(2) For want of supply beyond the city's control.
(3) For nonpayment of a service bill.
(4) On account of, or to prevent, fraud.
(5) For a violation by the customer of any provision of this article.
(6) Insufficiency of sewage treatment facility.
(7) Legal processes.
(8) Direction of public authorities.
(9) Acts of God.
(c) Other terminations. The city reserves the right to terminate the services granted by the city for any other reason other than those stated in this section by giving the consumer ten days' written notice of the date of termination, and further providing the consumer with a right to hearing prior to termination.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 9, 5-7-1996)
1061:
The city shall have the right from time to time, if necessary, to allocate water to the consumer.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 10, 5-7-1996)
1062:
(a) Plans and specifications for construction of water lines. The city shall have the right to specify the requirements, plans and specifications for construction of water lines in the city. All water lines constructed, or paid for, by the city, utility, contractor, consumer, owner or developer shall be constructed according to the plans and specifications established by the city for the construction of water lines in the city. No water line shall be covered without first being inspected and approved by the city.
(b) Right-of-way. Water lines may be extended along city streets which have sufficient dedicated right-of-way.
(c) Ownership of lines. All water lines built will become the property of the city.
(d) Water line extensions and increase in size of existing and/or new water lines to serve residential, commercial, and industrial development. This section applies to new residential subdivisions, industrial sites and commercial sites and to necessary extensions of existing and/or new water lines along existing public streets to reach those sites. The owner of the new development shall be required to pay the full cost for labor, materials, design, and all other cost of water line extensions. If the city determines that it is in the best interest of the city to increase the size of the existing water lines serving the new development, the owner of the new development shall be required to pay the full cost for labor, materials, design, and all other cost for the increase in the size of the existing water lines. Line construction must adhere strictly to adopted city specifications. Extensions and increase in size of existing and/or new water lines to a new development will be considered under the following conditions:
(1) Right-of-way. Sufficient dedicated right-of-way must be available along city streets required to access the development.
(2) [Zoning.] The developer must provide a letter from the zoning enforcement officer or his/her designee that the property has been properly zoned for the proposed use.
(3) Construction plans. The developer must provide the city with three copies of a plat or accurate drawing of the property to be served. Such plats or drawings shall contain the following information:
a. Location of the closest existing water line of the city which is of sufficient size to serve the property;
b. Location of the existing and proposed roads to serve the property;
c. Exact footage of water line that will have to be installed in order to serve the property;
d. Location of all water lines and appurtenances to be constructed in the area to be developed; and
e. Documentation that lines and appurtenances have been sized to meet the city's specifications for consumer demand and fire flows.
(4) Financial documentation. The developer must document financial ability to pay the cost of construction and must deposit required connection fees with the city.
(5) City approval. Once items in subsections (d)(1) through (4) of this section are completed, the request will be submitted to the city council for its approval.
(6) Construction by developer. Lines will normally be allowed to be constructed by the developer only within the development itself. In such instances, the developer must submit copies of construction plans conforming to city specifications to the city for review. During construction, the city will inspect work as necessary.
(7) Other items to be considered. Upon completion of construction by the developer, but prior to the initiation of water service the following must be done:
a. The city will conduct tests to ensure that completed water lines meet city specifications for pressure, flow and water quality.
b. The developer must post a deed conveying the water line, appurtenances thereto and any required permanent easements to the city.
c. The developer must post a surety bond, or letter of credit from any banking institution within the state with the city in the amount of ten percent of the total cost of the construction of such line, which such bond, or letter of credit, shall guarantee payment to the city for any repairs or maintenance needed in such line over a period of one year from the date of conveyance of such line.
d. The developer must furnish three copies of as-built water lines and appurtenances.
e. The developer must execute an affidavit prescribed by the city stating that the cost of all labor and materials has been paid; accompanied by copies of all invoices.
(Ord. No. 96-10, art. 11, 5-7-1996; Ord. No. 2-12-2007, § 1, 12-27-2007)
1064:
(a) Permit. A fire hydrant water use permit is required for each separate occasion where water will be taken from a hydrant. The permit will indicate the hydrant location, the date used and the estimated number of gallons.
(b) Metering. Except as approved by the city, all water taken from fire hydrants must be measured through the city's meter. A meter deposit of $50.00 is required each time the meter is used. This deposit will be refunded immediately upon return of the meter in good condition.
(c) Approved container. All tanks, tanker trucks, seed spraying trucks and other containers which will be filled with water must obtain an approved certificate of inspection for hydrant use which verifies that the container is equipped with a permanent approved air gap or reduced pressure zone backflow prevention device. The fee for inspection is $10.00 per vehicle and is good for a period of one year.
(d) Hoses and connections. Hoses connected to a fire hydrant for purposes other than filling an inspected and approved container shall not be submerged and/or left unsecured in a pool, pond, lake or container at any time while attached to the hydrant. A minimum air gap equal to two times the outlet diameter of the hose shall be maintained at all times above the pool or container overflow level. Under no condition will more than one of the 2½-inch connections on the fire hydrant be allowed for use at any time with each issued permit.
(e) Hydrant operation. Persons using fire hydrants will be instructed on proper hydrant use by the city. Any damage done to the hydrant will be the responsibility of the party using the hydrant.
(f) Billing. The party taking water from a hydrant will be billed directly by the city for water used at the standing rate for hydrant water use. No second-party billing will be made. Any water distributed from the hydrant at the city fire department must be paid for at the time of distribution. (See appendix A of Ordinance No. 96-10 for hydrant usage rates.)

1070:
For purposes of this article, the following definitions apply:
City means the City of Jackson.
Covered account means (i) An account that a financial institution or creditor offers or maintains, primarily for personal, family, or household purposes, that involves or is designed to permit multiple payments or transactions, such as a credit card account, mortgage loan, automobile loan, margin account, cell phone account, utility account, checking account, or savings account; and (ii) Any other account that the financial institution or creditor offers or maintains for which there is a reasonably foreseeable risk to customers or to the safety and soundness of the financial institution or creditor from identity theft, including financial, operational, compliance, reputation, or litigation risks.
Credit means the right granted by a creditor to a debtor to defer payment of debt or to incur debts and defer its payment or to purchase property or services and defer payment therefore.
Creditor means any person who regularly extends, renews, or continues credit; any person who regularly arranges for the extension, renewal, or continuation of credit; or any assignee of an original creditor who participates in the decision to extend, renew, or continue credit and includes utility companies and telecommunications companies.
Customer means a person that has a covered account with a creditor.
Identity theft means a fraud committed or attempted using identifying information of another person without authority.
Person means a natural person, a corporation, government or governmental subdivision or agency, trust, estate, partnership, cooperative, or association.
Personal identifying information means a person's credit card account information, debit card information bank account information and drivers' license information and for a natural person includes their social security number, mother's birth name, and date of birth.
Red flag means a pattern, practice, or specific activity that indicates the possible existence of identity theft.
Service provider means a person that provides a service directly to the city.
(Ord. No. 01-10-2008, § 1, 10-21-2008)

(a) Access to customer accounts shall be password protected and shall be limited to authorized city personnel.

(a) In the event that credit card payments that are made over the Internet are processed through a third party service provider, such third party service provider shall certify that it has an adequate identity theft prevention program in place that is applicable to such payments.

1075:
All employees responsible for or involved in the process of opening a covered account, restoring a covered account, or accepting payment for a covered account shall check for red flags as indicators of possible identity theft and such red flags may include:
(1) Alerts from consumer reporting agencies, fraud detection agencies or service providers. Examples of alerts include but are not limited to:
a. A fraud or active duty alert that is included with a consumer report;
b. A notice of credit freeze in response to a request for a consumer report;
c. A notice of address discrepancy provided by a consumer reporting agency;
d. Indications of a pattern of activity in a consumer report that is inconsistent with the history and usual pattern of activity of an applicant or customer such as:
(i) A recent and significant increase in the volume of inquiries;
(ii) An unusual number of recently established credit relationships;
(iii) A material change in the use of credit, especially with respect to recently established credit relationships; or
(iv) An account that was closed for cause or identified for abuse of account privileges by a financial institution or creditor.
(2) Suspicious documents. Examples of suspicious documents include:
a. Documents provided for identification that appear to be altered or forged;
b. Identification on which the photograph or physical description is inconsistent with the appearance of the applicant or customer;
c. Identification on which the information is inconsistent with information provided by the applicant or customer;
d. Identification on which the information is inconsistent with readily accessible information that is on file with the financial institution or creditor, such as a signature card or a recent check; or
e. An application that appears to have been altered or forged, or appears to have been destroyed and reassembled.
(3) Suspicious personal identification, such as suspicious address change. Examples of suspicious identifying information include:
a. Personal identifying information that is inconsistent with external information sources used by the financial institution or creditor. For example:
(i) The address does not match any address in the consumer report; or
(ii) The social security number (SSN) has not been issued, or is listed on the Social Security Administration's Death Master File.
b. Personal identifying information provided by the customer is not consistent with other personal identifying information provided by the customer, such as a lack of correlation between the SSN range and date of birth.
c. Personal identifying information or a phone number or address is associated with known fraudulent applications or activities as indicated by internal or third-party sources used by the financial institution or creditor.
d. Other information provided, such as fictitious mailing address, mail drop addresses, jail addresses, invalid phone numbers, pager numbers or answering services, is associated with fraudulent activity.
e. The SSN provided is the same as that submitted by other applicants or customers.
f. The address or telephone number provided is the same as or similar to the account number or telephone number submitted by an unusually large number of applicants or customers.
g. The applicant or customer fails to provide all required personal identifying information on an application or in response to notification that the application is incomplete.
h. Personal identifying information is not consistent with personal identifying information that is on file with the financial institution or creditor.
i. The applicant or customer cannot provide authenticating information beyond that which generally would be available from a wallet or consumer report.
(4) Unusual use of or suspicious activity relating to a covered account. Examples of suspicious activity include:
a. Shortly following the notice of a change of address for an account, city receives a request for the addition of authorized users on the account.
b. A new revolving credit account is used in a manner commonly associated with known patterns of fraud patterns. For example:
(i) The customer fails to make the first payment or makes an initial payment but no subsequent payments.
c. An account is used in a manner that is not consistent with established patterns of activity on the account. There is, for example:
(i) Nonpayment when there is no history of late or missed payments;
(ii) A material change in purchasing or spending patterns.
d. An account that has been inactive for a long period of time is used (taking into consideration the type of account, the expected pattern of usage and other relevant factors).
e. Mail sent to the customer is returned repeatedly as undeliverable although transactions continue to be conducted in connection with the customer's account.
f. The city is notified that the customer is not receiving paper account statements.
g. The city is notified of unauthorized charges or transactions in connection with a customer's account.
h. The city is notified by a customer, law enforcement or another person that it has opened a fraudulent account for a person engaged in identity theft.
(5) Notice from customers, law enforcement, victims or other reliable sources regarding possible identity theft or phishing relating to covered accounts
(Ord. No. 01-10-2008, § 1, 10-21-2008)

The administrative officer shall carefully review all site plans and make decisions based upon this article and any other ordinance provision of the city or state or federal law or regulation. Any party who disagrees with a decision made by the administrative officer shall have a right to review before the tree board. The following rules for hearings and decisions shall apply:
(1) When deciding whether or not to approve a commercial site plan, the administrative officer shall consider only site plans which have been submitted to the planning and zoning office. If the administrative officer reaches any decision other than approval, he must notify the applicant in writing that the applicant's site plan for trees has been disapproved by the administrative officer and the specific reasons for the unfavorable decision. The applicant will be notified that he is entitled to a hearing before the administrative officer upon request.
(2) An applicant's request for a review hearing before the administrative officer must be in writing and must be delivered to the planning and zoning office within seven days of the date that the administrative officer mailed to the applicant a notice of an unfavorable decision. Upon the filing of such a request for hearing, the administrative officer shall conduct a hearing within seven days of the filing of the request. At the hearing, the administrative officer shall conduct the proceedings. The applicant will be entitled to appear and present relevant evidence. The administrative officer may also hear from any interested parties and consider any relevant facts, provided the applicant has an ample opportunity to examine same. The applicant shall be entitled to be represented by counsel. The administrative officer shall not have subpoena power. Minutes of the meeting, including a tape recording, shall be made by the administrative officer.
(3) At the hearing, the administrative officer may ask questions of the applicant and may attempt to resolve the issue(s) leading to the unfavorable decision by stipulation. After the hearing has been concluded the administrative officer will issue a decision in writing within 48 hours and deliver a copy to the applicant by regular mail. The decision will state specific reasons for any ruling other than approval of the tree site plan. The administrative officer may issue an approval of a site plan as amended by stipulation of the applicant, he may approve the plan as originally filed, or he may disapprove and state its specific reasons.
(4) An applicant may appeal any unfavorable ruling to the tree board, which shall conduct a de novo hearing. The applicant's rights will remain the same as in paragraph (2) above. An appeal to the tree board shall be in writing, and it shall include a copy of the administrative officer's decision and shall state specifically those portions of the administrative officer's decision with which the applicant disagrees. The appeal must be filed with the administrative officer within 30 days of the date of the administrative officer's decision. The tree board shall hear the appeal at the next regular tree board meeting after the appeal is filed. The decision of the tree board shall be issued in writing within 48 hours after the hearing and a copy shall be mailed to the applicant. Any decision that does not approve the site plan shall state specific reasons for the decision.
(5) The following rules of procedure shall apply in those cases where the mayor and city council or administrative officer exercises the power to cause the removal of any dead or diseased trees on private property, pursuant to the authority of section 70-26:
a. When it is determined that a tree or trees constitute a hazard to life or property or harbor insects or disease which constitute a potential threat to other trees within the city, the mayor and city council or administrative officer shall issue a written notice to the owners and persons in possession of the property stating the location of the tree or trees and the reason that removal is required. Such notice shall be in writing and shall notify the owners and persons in possession that they are to perform all removal and dispose of all debris within 60 days of the receipt of such notice. The notice will also state that any interested party has the right to demand a hearing before the tree board within seven days after service of the notice. A notice shall be considered served upon the owners or persons in possession when actually received by such interested party either by personal delivery or certified mail, return receipt requested, addressed and properly posted to the last known mailing address of the owner or person in possession. If such interested person cannot be found after diligent search or attempted delivery of the notice by certified mail is returned undelivered for any reason, notice shall be considered delivered when advertised in the official organ in the county for two consecutive weeks and a copy of the notice is conspicuously posted upon the premises which are the subject matter of the notice. The date of delivery in such cases shall be the later of the date of posting or the date of the publication of the last of the two advertisements.
b. If any owner or person in possession of the premises notifies the mayor and city council or administrative officer in writing of an objection to the planned action, a hearing will be scheduled before any action is taken upon the property in question. The hearing shall be conducted before the tree board, and the decision of the tree board can be appealed to the city council. 1115:
(a) Qualifications. All members of the tree board must be residents of the city.
(b) Officers. The membership of the board shall elect by majority vote a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and a secretary. The chairperson shall preside, the vice-chairperson shall preside in the absence of the chairperson, and the secretary shall be responsible for keeping records of the actions of the board and preparing and delivering decisions.
(c) Meetings and voting. All voting on decisions shall be by roll call vote and the results of the voting shall be kept by the secretary in the minutes. All votes shall be by majority vote, and the member acting as chairperson shall be allowed to vote. There must be a majority quorum present and voting in order to conduct any business. Members shall adhere to the same rules as to disqualifications and conflicts of interest as the city council. The chairperson shall set meeting times and places, so long as the meeting place is within the city. The board shall establish the time of its meetings by the giving of at least 48 hours' notice to members and all interested parties and it shall comply with the state's open meetings law (O.C.G.A. § 50-14-1 et seq.).
(d) Appointments. Members shall be appointed by the mayor and the city council. They shall serve at the pleasure of the mayor and council. The members shall be appointed for three-year staggered terms. The board shall be comprised of three members. They shall serve without compensation, but may apply to the city council for reimbursement for any actual expenses incurred in their service, with the approval of the chairperson of the tree board.
(Ord. No. 96-36, § XVIII, 11-18-1996; Ord. of 4-6-1999)
